functions.label: line through P with your slope

widget.instructions: Point P marks the instant asked about. The slider draws a line through P with any trial slope: the tangent just touches the curve.

stem: A ball's position is x = {{a}}t² + {{b}}t (x in m, t in s), so its x–t graph curves upward.
What is its instantaneous velocity at t = {{t1}} s?

hints.text: On a curved x–t graph, which line's slope is the velocity at P?
The tangent at P: the derivative dx/dt at that instant.

average-for-instantaneous.text: That is the average velocity from t = 0, x ÷ t. The instantaneous velocity is the slope of the tangent at that instant.

position-for-velocity.text: That is the position at t = {{t1}} s. Velocity is how fast the position changes: the slope.

dimension-mismatch.text: Check the unit: the answer is a velocity.

generic.text: Velocity is the slope of the tangent: dx/dt at that instant.

workedSolution.text: At t = {{t1}} s: v = {{ans}} m/s (the average from t = 0 is only {{avg}} m/s).

average-for-instantaneous.front: Instantaneous velocity on a curved x–t graph?
average-for-instantaneous.back: The slope of the tangent at that instant, not x ÷ t.

position-for-velocity.front: On an x–t graph, is the height of the curve the velocity?
position-for-velocity.back: No. The height is the position; the slope is the velocity.

generic.back: v = dx/dt, the slope of the tangent at that instant.

accessibility.altText: A curved x–t graph with a point P at t = {{t1}} s.
accessibility.nonDragAlternative: The graph is for reading; type your answer in the box.
